issues.body: `is_absolute_iri` now checks a valid scheme and a blacklist of characters, but that is not sufficient to validate an RFC 3987 IRI as required by expansion step 15.4. For example, `http://example.com/%ZZ` and a trailing bare `%` contain none of the blacklisted characters and are therefore accepted as datatype IRIs even though their percent-encoding is malformed. Other RFC 3987 structural/code-point constraints are likewise not represented. This makes the new `datatype_iri_with_a_space_is_rejected` test a narrow witness rather than evidence for the documented general obligation, and can let invalid typed values expand successfully.
issues.fix_hint: Use a real IRI parser/validator appropriate to RFC 3987, or implement complete validation (including percent-encoding and allowed Unicode ranges) at the datatype check. Add focused negative tests for malformed percent escapes such as `%ZZ` and `%`, plus a positive Unicode IRI case to prevent over-rejection.
issues.title: Datatype IRI validation still accepts malformed IRIs

verdict.summary: The negative-test runner wiring and non-vacuity guards are well structured, but the datatype-IRI fix is incomplete relative to the JSON-LD requirement and the PR's own claim. It rejects a small character class rather than validating IRI syntax, so malformed absolute-looking datatype IRIs still pass.
